title: Invited: The Magnificent Seven Challenges and Opportunities in Domain-Specific Accelerator Design for Autonomous Systems
problem: Domain-specific accelerator designers encounter recurring pitfalls when entering unfamiliar application domains that hinder development progress. These common challenges appear across diverse domains including ML, genomics, and autonomous systems but lack systematic characterization.
motivation: With Moore's Law and Dennard Scaling ending, domain-specific acceleration is critical for computing innovation, but architects need guidance on common pitfalls to successfully design accelerators for new domains.
method: The paper reviews lessons learned from building custom hardware accelerators (computer chips designed for specific tasks) in different fields. It uses autonomous systems as a detailed example to identify seven problems that recur whenever engineers design these specialized chips for new applications. These same pitfalls keep appearing in machine learning, genomics, and other domains, explaining why accelerator design is difficult and suggesting what challenges to anticipate.
key_novelty: The paper identifies seven recurring problems that appear whenever engineers design custom hardware accelerators—the same pitfalls show up across machine learning, genomics, and autonomous systems.
contributions: Identifies the Magnificent Seven Challenges that commonly hinder domain-specific accelerator development
Examines accelerator design challenges through the lens of autonomous systems
Provides guidance for architects to navigate common pitfalls and opportunities in novel application domains
limitations: As an invited position paper, the work focuses on identifying challenges rather than proposing concrete solutions or providing experimental validation.
